headline: Chips and Energy Lead a Soft Tape as Software and Financials Sag
body_html:
Stocks were leaning lower at midday, with 364 of the 664 names we track falling and 296 rising. That split hides a sharp divide underneath. Semiconductors, up 1.01%, and energy, up 0.89%, led, while financials, down 1.91%, and software, down 1.35%, were the heaviest drags. Prices are not final.

The dominant theme is rotation inside technology, not a broad risk-on move. Optical names ran, with Coherent up 5.67% and Applied Optoelectronics up 5.47%, as investors positioned ahead of a major AI chip earnings report and a closely watched Anthropic public debut. Software was sold hard, with Asana off 5.20% and HubSpot off 5.15%. Tokyo Electron slid 5.47%, a sign that the chip rally is selective.

The standout mover was Forgent Power Solutions, up 10.67%, while AECOM gained 8.11% in a strong showing for industrial and infrastructure names. Energy firmness fits a backdrop of renewed Gulf tension. Into the close, watch whether chip leadership holds, whether financials stop sliding, and how positioning sets up for Wednesday, November 18.

briefs.headline: Power and Engineering Names Surge
briefs.body: Forgent Power Solutions jumped 10.67% and AECOM rose 8.11%, the two biggest gains in our universe so far. Industrials as a group were up a more modest 0.37%, so the move looks driven by individual stocks rather than a sector-wide push.

briefs.headline: Software Takes the Brunt of Selling
briefs.body: Software fell 1.35% as a group, with Asana down 5.20%, HubSpot down 5.15%, Freshworks down 4.54% and Amplitude down 4.39%. The slide comes as investors weigh the arrival of a large AI IPO that could pull attention and capital toward other corners of tech.

briefs.headline: Optical Suppliers Rally, Chip Equipment Lags
briefs.body: Coherent gained 5.67% and Applied Optoelectronics 5.47%, extending a push into AI-linked networking hardware ahead of a major chip earnings report. Tokyo Electron went the other way, down 5.47%, so the semiconductor strength is not reaching every part of the supply chain.

briefs.headline: Gulf Flare-Up Keeps Energy Bid
briefs.body: Reports of Iranian attacks on a US radar system in Bahrain and a second tanker incident near Oman's Khasab kept geopolitical risk in focus. Energy was up 0.89%, among the better sectors. Traders will watch for any shift in the diplomatic talks.

briefs.headline: Consumer Split: Amer Sports Up, Capri Down
briefs.body: Amer Sports climbed 7.41% and MINISO rose 5.75%, while Capri Holdings fell 7.30%, the largest drop in our list. Nike's first investor day in nine years put its turnaround back in view. The consumer sector was flat overall, down 0.01%.

briefs.headline: UK Labor Cools; Rupee Hits Seven-Month High
briefs.body: UK pay growth slowed and job vacancies fell to their lowest since 2021, a sign of loosening in the labor market. Elsewhere, strong inflows and fewer short bets lifted India's rupee to a seven-month high.
